rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 42 (Texas 42) - Quick Rules 1.1 Overview 1.2 Setup 1.3 Bidding 1.4 Gameplay 1.5 Scoring 1.6 Tile Ranking 42 (Texas 42) - Quick Rules Overview Players: 4 players (in fixed partnerships, sitting opposite each other). Equipment: A standard double-six domino set (28 tiles). Objective: Be the first team to reach 7 points (marks) by winning tricks and "count" tiles. Setup Shuffle all tiles face down. Each player draws 7 tiles. Play proceeds clockwise. Bidding Starting with the dealer, each player makes exactly one bid or passes. The minimum bid is 30 . The maximum bid is 42 (or a "Mark"). A bid represents the number of points the team expects to win in the round. The highest bidder declares Trumps (a suit like "Fours", "Ones", or "Doubles" / "No Trump"). Gameplay The highest bidder leads the first tile. Following Suit: Players must follow the suit of the high end of the tile led (e.g., if a 5-3 is led, players must play a "Five", unless Fives are trump). If a player cannot follow suit, they may play a trump or any other tile. The highest tile of the suit led wins the trick, unless a trump is played. The winner of the trick leads the next one. Scoring There are 42 total points available in each round: Tricks: Each trick won is worth 1 point (7 points total). Count Tiles: Tiles with pips totaling 5 or 10 are worth their face value: 5-0, 4-1, 3-2 are worth 5 points each. 6-4, 5-5 are worth 10 points each. Round Results: If the bidding team meets or exceeds its bid, it scores 1 mark toward the game total. If they fail, the opposing team scores the mark. Tile Ranking Within the Trump suit: The Double is the highest tile, followed by others in descending order. In a non-trump suit: The Double is also the highest, followed by the others.
